plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual consequential damages exclusion with direct-damage carve-ins, and an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, and IP infringement. Check mutuality and that carve-outs survive the cap; likely compliant.

No indemnification section appears in the outline (Section 20 is absent although Sections 9.3 and 19.4 cross-reference Section 20.5 IP infringement remedies). Confirm the missing Section 20; if truly absent, flag as missing and propose a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity with a narrow Customer indemnity.

Second Section 12.4 imposes a 24-month, unlimited-territory competition ban on Customer — squarely prohibited. Note it directly contradicts Section 12.3, which disclaims any non-compete; propose deletion and reliance on 12.3.

Section 12.3 preserves supplier freedom, but Section 7.2 (first) requires Customer to disclose and match competing offers before engaging another provider — a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal. Assess 7.2 as the deviation; avoid double-flagging the MFN aspect if handled under MFN.

First Section 7.2 obliges Customer to disclose and match more favourable third-party offers — an MFN running against us, contrary to Section 12.3's disclaimer. Flag under whichever of MFN/EXCLUSIVITY best fits; do not redline the same sentence twice unless both are independently breached.

First Section 12.4 bars Customer from soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee for 24 months with no general-advertising carve-out and regardless of how the employee applies — beyond the narrow, time-limited fallback. Section 12.3's general-recruitment freedom conflicts and can support the redline.

Section 9 contains only cause-based, insolvency, and security/service-level termination rights (note Section 9.4 is absent from the outline); no convenience right for Customer, and Section 2.1 expressly denies termination rights. Verify no convenience clause exists before treating as missing.

Section 8.2 gives a 30-day non-renewal window plus a 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension; Section 8.3 caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant; note any wording shortfalls in the rationale only.

Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts — outside the accepted list — while Section 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts. Flag the conflict and align governing law to New York consistent with 28.2.

Section 24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment; 24.4 bars Vendor termination or repricing on Customer change of control. Likely compliant — do not flag clauses favouring us.

Section 14.1 preserves Customer ownership of data and pre-existing IP, but Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, term-limited licence — contrary to owning what we pay for. Note tension with Sections 13.2 and 14.3's perpetual licence.

Sections 13.1–13.3 cover Affiliates and contractors, grant a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology, and limit revocation to material uncured breach with cure. Main tension is the revocable Deliverable licence in Section 14.2 — address there rather than duplicating.

Section 22 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months with 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, at Vendor's cost unless a 5% underpayment is found, with system/data access carve-outs. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages, early-termination penalty, or interest-penalty clause payable by Customer is apparent; Section 2.1's take-or-pay is the closest economic penalty but belongs under MINCOMMIT. Check Sections 7.3 and 22.2 for cost-shifting before concluding absent.

Section 19 provides professional-services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, whole term for hosted Services), malicious-code and legal-compliance warranties, with repair/re-perform plus refund and termination remedy in 19.4 that is expressly non-exclusive. Likely compliant.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5M cyber cover for the term plus one year; 18.2 adds certificates, primacy, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Present and likely compliant.

Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per-year, three-year take-or-pay commitment expressly without reduction or termination rights — a walk-away term and inconsistent with Section 12.3's disclaimer of minimum-volume commitments.

Section 10 addresses access cessation, Deliverable delivery and refunds, and references an 'agreed transition period', but no express data-return/export obligation or transition-assistance services appear (Section 11, cross-referenced in 16.5, is absent from the outline). Verify before marking missing.
